He shook his fist in Parliament and called them villains, over ships worth more at the bottom of the sea.
You see, in Victorian Britain, shipowners have a nasty trick.
They over-insure rotting old ships, then cram them with cargo until they're barely floating.
If a ship makes it, they get rich. If it sinks, they get even richer.
Then an MP named Samuel Plimsoll pushes a simple fix. Paint a line on every hull. Water over the line? The ship stays home.
The shipowners just laugh. "A line of paint? On MY ship?"
And it gets worse. Plenty of them sit in Parliament.
So when the safety bill gets dropped, Plimsoll snaps.
He stamps his foot, slams his protest on the table, shakes his fist, and yells, "I am determined to unmask the villains!"
The Speaker orders him to take it back. He refuses.
Meanwhile, up in the gallery, his wife is calmly handing copies of his protest to the reporters.
The papers print every word, and one crowd jokes, "If Mr Plimsoll is mad, he should bite a few more MPs!"
Within weeks, Parliament caves. A year later, British ships have to wear his line.
And that rubber stripe around gym shoes? It looked so much like his line, they got his name. Plimsolls.
